With a strong commitment to fostering a sense of belonging, Mi Centro provides essential resources that support individuals and families in navigating various aspects of life, from educational programs to health services. Our new facility serves as a welcoming space where community members can connect, learn, and grow.

What sets Mi Centro apart is its holistic approach to community service, focusing on the unique needs of the Hispanic community while promoting inclusivity and engagement across all cultural backgrounds. Our expertly designed programs not only address immediate needs but also encourage long-term development, empowering individuals to achieve their personal and professional goals. By participating in Mi Centro’s offerings, community members benefit from tailored support, networking opportunities, and access to resources that enhance their quality of life and strengthen the community as a whole.

data.Title: Chabad at the University of Wisconsin
data.Description:
Chabad at the University of Wisconsin in Madison, WI, is a dynamic Jewish organization dedicated to enriching the lives of students, alumni, parents, and the broader university community. Rooted in the Chabad-Lubavitch philosophy, it fosters a vibrant environment built on principles of wisdom, comprehension, and knowledge, guiding individuals to a deeper understanding and appreciation of Jewish life and values. This approach emphasizes personal growth, spiritual connection, and a strong sense of Jewish identity.

The center provides a welcoming and inclusive space, emphasizing friendship, tradition, holidays, joy, and Jewish pride. It offers a diverse range of programs and services tailored to the university setting, including High Holiday observances, communal Shabbat dinners, and extensive online learning resources covering Jewish practice, ethics, and mysticism. Chabad at UW is committed to connecting individuals to their Jewish heritage, offering spiritual guidance, educational opportunities, and a strong sense of belonging, ensuring that every Jew feels supported and celebrated within the Madison community.

data.Title: Chabad Madison
data.Description:
Chabad Madison is a vibrant Jewish organization serving the Madison, Dane County, and South-Central Wisconsin communities. As a local center of the global Chabad-Lubavitch movement, it is deeply committed to "Ahavat Yisrael," fostering unconditional love and concern for every Jew, regardless of their background or affiliation. The organization applies the profound Chabad philosophy, which emphasizes wisdom, comprehension, and knowledge, to guide individuals in understanding their heritage and connecting with their spiritual purpose.

Chabad Madison offers a diverse array of programs and services designed to enrich Jewish life and promote spiritual growth. These include educational initiatives like the Chabad Hebrew School and the Jewish Learning Institute, fostering Jewish knowledge and identity for all ages. The center also provides opportunities for communal engagement through Shabbat dinners, synagogue services, and specialized groups such as the Jewish Women's Circle and programs for Young Jewish Professionals and Chabad at UW. Through these offerings, Chabad Madison empowers individuals to explore, practice, and experience their Jewish heritage in a welcoming and supportive environment.

data.Title: Chapel of Faith Anglican Church Madison
data.Description:
Chapel of Faith Anglican Church Madison serves as a vibrant spiritual home for individuals and families in Madison, WI, seeking to deepen their faith and connect with a welcoming community. Rooted in the rich traditions of Anglican worship, the church offers a sacred space for prayer, reflection, and the celebration of the Holy Eucharist. Its mission is to foster spiritual growth, uphold biblical teachings, and provide a supportive environment where members can explore their faith journey.

Committed to both timeless liturgy and contemporary relevance, Chapel of Faith Anglican Church Madison emphasizes thoughtful preaching, beautiful music, and the sacraments as central to its spiritual life. Beyond weekly services, the church actively engages in community outreach and offers various programs for spiritual formation, fellowship, and service, aiming to embody Christ's love in Madison and beyond. It stands as a beacon of faith, inviting all to experience the grace and fellowship found within its doors.

data.Title: Christ Presbyterian Church
data.Description:
Christ Presbyterian Church in Madison, WI, boasts a rich history spanning over 170 years, rooted deeply in Presbyterian and Reformed traditions. Situated in a beautiful, recently renovated facility overlooking Lake Mendota, CPC is committed to being Christ-centered and fostering an ecumenical fellowship that welcomes people from all backgrounds and experiences. Whether you are a lifelong Christian, new to faith, or exploring, the church meets individuals with an open heart and a curious mind, learning together to put God's love into action.

CPC offers two distinct weekly worship services: a Contemporary Service featuring a band with diverse instrumentation, and a Classical Service led by a choir with organ, piano, and often brass and strings. Both services are intentionally liturgical and creative, designed to inspire hope, deepen connection with God, and build community. 

Beyond worship, Christ Presbyterian Church actively engages with the Madison community through partnerships with numerous local organizations, including the Community Immigration Law Center, Nehemiah, MOSES Madison, and the Madison Public Schools Foundation. The church's inviting space is also available for community use, reflecting its dedication to serving and connecting with its neighbors.

data.Title: City Church Madison
data.Description:
City Church Madison is a vibrant spiritual community located in Madison, WI, dedicated to providing a welcoming environment where individuals can connect with Jesus and engage in life-giving fellowship. The church emphasizes creating a space for authentic encounters with the Holy Spirit, fostering spiritual growth, and encouraging members to discover and utilize their unique gifts for God's glory.

With a core philosophy of "come as you are," City Church Madison extends an open invitation to everyone, regardless of their background or current life stage. They host regular Sunday services at 8:30 AM and 11 AM, offering opportunities for worship, teaching, and community connection. Additionally, the church provides a midweek spiritual touchpoint with Tuesday night prayer sessions at 6:30 PM.

Beyond services, City Church Madison is committed to building a supportive community where individuals can grow in faith and purpose. They offer various avenues for engagement, including ministries, staff support, and opportunities to learn more about their mission and values. The church strives to be a place where every person feels valued and empowered on their spiritual journey.

data.Title: Civic Media
data.Description:
Civic Media is revolutionizing local radio in Wisconsin by providing communities with essential news, engaging conversations, and curated music. With a state-wide radio network, Civic Media focuses on local stories that matter, from county board meetings to high school sports, ensuring that every corner of Wisconsin is represented. By prioritizing regional and state news over national headlines, Civic Media fosters a sense of community and connection among listeners, empowering them to engage with the issues that affect their daily lives.

At Civic Media, transparency is key. The organization believes in sharing its mission and values with the audience, reinforcing the importance of democracy and open dialogue. With a diverse range of programming available across multiple platforms—including live broadcasts, podcasts, and streaming services—Civic Media ensures that listeners can stay informed and entertained wherever they are. By revitalizing local media services that have been neglected, Civic Media is committed to enriching the lives of Wisconsinites and strengthening the fabric of their communities.

data.Title: Clean Lakes Alliance
data.Description:
Clean Lakes Alliance is a dedicated nonprofit organization based in Madison, WI, committed to enhancing the water quality of the Yahara River Watershed's lakes, streams, and wetlands. Operating as a unique partnership, the Alliance collaborates with diverse stakeholders, including government agencies, community groups, and property owners, to build upon decades of conservation efforts. Their primary goal is to raise community awareness, advocate for the welfare of the lakes, and secure essential funding for restoration and protection initiatives.

The organization champions watershed stewardship for the benefit of all, driven by a vision of healthy waters and a thriving community. A core focus is the reduction of phosphorus pollution, the leading cause of poor water clarity, harmful algal blooms, and beach closures. Clean Lakes Alliance employs a strategic framework that prioritizes phosphorus reduction from both urban and rural sources through innovative solutions and improved land management.

Through these comprehensive strategies, Clean Lakes Alliance fosters community engagement through education, volunteer programs, and monitoring efforts to mobilize support for the lakes. They work tirelessly to ensure the long-term health and enjoyment of Madison's cherished waterways, embodying values of optimism, respect for water, collaboration, and science-backed decisions.

data.Title: College Library
data.Description:
College Library, situated in Helen C. White Hall at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serves as a dynamic academic hub, particularly for undergraduate students. It provides a comprehensive array of resources and services meticulously designed to support diverse learning needs and research pursuits. The library offers extensive collections, encompassing both physical and electronic materials, complemented by specialized services such as course reserves and tailored research guides.

Distinguishing itself beyond conventional library offerings, College Library emphasizes modern learning environments and cutting-edge technological access. Students can choose from a variety of study spaces, ranging from quiet individual zones to collaborative active learning classrooms. The library also features advanced technology services, including equipment for checkout like laptops and projectors, dedicated computer labs, and specialized facilities such as recording booths and media studios. A unique offering is its Tool Library, providing practical resources for various projects. College Library is dedicated to fostering an inclusive and supportive environment, ensuring accessibility and promoting academic success for the entire UW-Madison community.

data.Title: Common Wealth Development Inc
data.Description:
Common Wealth Development Inc. (CWD) is a dedicated community organization in Madison, WI, committed to preserving neighborhood vitality and fostering a healthier, more equitable metropolitan area. For over 46 years, CWD has been at the forefront of preventing violence and decreasing health inequities through a multi-faceted approach to community development.

CWD's comprehensive initiatives span three core areas. Their Economic Development programs empower local entrepreneurs by offering affordable business incubation spaces and crucial support, having successfully aided 33 small businesses. Through Workforce Development, CWD equips both youth and adults with vital skills in financial literacy, job readiness, and entrepreneurial leadership, positively impacting hundreds of individuals. Additionally, their Housing Development efforts provide safe, stable, and affordable housing opportunities for renters and aspiring homeowners, managing a portfolio of 176 units.

By integrating these essential services, Common Wealth Development Inc. actively builds stronger communities, enhances economic resilience, and creates sustainable pathways to stability and success for residents across Madison.

data.Title: Community Action Coalition For South Central Wisconsin, Inc.
data.Description:
Community Action Coalition For South Central Wisconsin, Inc. (CACSCW) is a dedicated nonprofit organization committed to ending poverty and fostering social and economic security across Dane, Jefferson, and Waukesha Counties. With over 50 years of experience, CACSCW works to transform systems and apply innovative, targeted strategies to address the root causes of poverty, helping individuals and families achieve stability and thrive. The organization firmly believes that food and housing insecurity are public health crises, striving to ensure everyone has a place to call home and food on the table.

CACSCW provides comprehensive services focused on critical areas such as housing security, food security, and broader community programs. Their housing initiatives offer support to individuals seeking stable and reliable shelter through dedicated case managers, while food security efforts ensure access to nutritious food for community members and support local food pantries via their food bank. Additionally, they offer vital community programs including mental health and trauma recovery support, financial literacy, and career resources, alongside comprehensive "Where to Find" guides to connect residents with essential local resources.

Founded in 1966 as part of President Lyndon B. Johnson’s ‘War on Poverty,’ CACSCW has a rich history of empowering low-income communities. They continue to evolve their approach, collaborating with strong partners to identify and act in areas of greatest need, ensuring people can overcome challenges and live with dignity.

data.Title: Community Shares of Wisconsin
data.Description:
Community Shares of Wisconsin is a vital organization based in Madison, WI, dedicated to strengthening the local social and environmental justice movement. For 50 years, CSW has brought together over 70 member nonprofits, raising essential funds and awareness to address systemic issues like racism, ableism, classism, and transphobia. They prioritize identifying and changing policies and practices that perpetuate inequality, working to tackle the root causes of socio-economic disparities for lasting community change.

Through innovative programs like The Big Share and Workplace Giving, Community Shares of Wisconsin empowers its member organizations who are on the front lines in Dane County and across Wisconsin. Their collaborative model emphasizes equity, ensuring member nonprofits have a voice in decisions and build partnerships to amplify community voices. CSW envisions a future with clean water and air, access to family-supporting jobs, and safe, thriving communities for all, actively working to protect rights and build a sustainable future.

data.Title: Congregation Shaarei Shamayim
data.Description:
Congregation Shaarei Shamayim in Madison, WI, is a vibrant Jewish community affiliated with both the Jewish Reconstructionist movement and Aleph: Alliance for Jewish Renewal. Dedicated to fostering a joyful and inclusive environment, the congregation offers diverse opportunities for spiritual growth, learning, and community engagement. Members participate in regular Shabbat services, holiday celebrations, and Torah study, with an emphasis on participatory and egalitarian practices that blend creativity with tradition.

The congregation provides comprehensive programming for all ages, including the Gesher creative Jewish educational program for children and teens, weekly Hebrew tutoring, and an innovative Bnei Mitzvah program. Adults can deepen their Jewish knowledge through various education classes and connect with others in havurot (fellowship groups). Beyond worship and education, Congregation Shaarei Shamayim is committed to tikkun olam, actively engaging in social action initiatives and promoting diversity, equity, and inclusivity within its welcoming community. The Rabbi also offers pastoral care and officiates life cycle events, supporting members through all stages of life.

data.Title: Dane Arts
data.Description:
Dane Arts is a pivotal agency within the Dane County Government dedicated to enriching the cultural landscape of Wisconsin through the promotion of arts, culture, and local history. With a mission to engage participation and inspire expressive living, Dane Arts serves as a vital resource for residents and visitors alike. The organization spearheads numerous initiatives, including grant programs, community mural projects, and local markets that showcase the talents of over 100 individual artists. By fostering collaborations and supporting the creative sector, Dane Arts enhances community connections and celebrates the unique heritage of Dane County.

What sets Dane Arts apart is its commitment to inclusivity and excellence in artistic expression, backed by nearly five decades of community service. The organization not only supports artists and arts organizations but also emphasizes the economic impact of the arts, highlighting that nearly $350 million flows into the local economy through cultural initiatives. By providing technical assistance and advocacy, Dane Arts empowers citizens to share their stories and creativity, ensuring that the vibrant cultural legacy of Dane County continues to thrive.

data.Title: Dane Buy Local, Inc.
data.Description:
Dane Buy Local, Inc. is a dedicated non-profit organization based in Madison, WI, committed to championing locally owned businesses through advocacy, education, and collaboration. Established in 2004, the organization operates on the vision that thriving local businesses lead to thriving communities. Its core values emphasize inclusivity, sustainability, and prosperity with purpose, fostering a collaborative environment where members uplift each other to strengthen collective impact.

The organization provides vital support to independent businesses, offering educational opportunities, networking events like Lunch & Learns and multi-chamber coffee connections, and a comprehensive local business guide. Dane Buy Local also plays a crucial role in community development, as demonstrated by its administration of $28 million in small business grants during the pandemic, supporting the economic resilience of Dane County. By promoting local ownership and purchasing, Dane Buy Local helps build social and economic capital, ensuring a better quality of life and a vibrant local ecosystem for future generations in Madison and the surrounding area.

data.Title: Dane County Humane Society’s Wildlife Center
data.Description:
Dane County Humane Society’s Wildlife Center, located in Madison, WI, provides critical specialized care and treatment for thousands of injured, ill, or orphaned wild animals annually. Established in 2002, the center has grown significantly, having cared for over 50,000 animals since its inception. Its primary mission is to rehabilitate these animals with the ultimate goal of releasing them back into their natural habitats, contributing to the health and biodiversity of the local ecosystem.

The Wildlife Center accepts over 150 different species, including native birds, reptiles, amphibians, and most mammals, filling a vital need for wildlife rehabilitation in the community. This extensive work is made possible through the dedication of its staff, interns, and a large network of trained volunteers who provide the majority of daily animal care. As a non-profit, the center relies entirely on community support and donations to fund its operations, ensuring that every animal receives the best possible chance at recovery and a successful return to the wild.

data.Title: Dane County Humane Society Thrift Store
data.Description:
Dane County Humane Society Thrift Store operates two vibrant locations in Madison, WI, serving as a crucial funding source for the Dane County Humane Society (DCHS). These thrift stores directly support DCHS's vital mission to help people and animals by providing refuge, healing, and new beginnings for thousands of companion animals, exotic species, barnyard animals, and injured wildlife annually. Shoppers can explore an extensive and ever-changing inventory, with over 20,000 unique items available at any given time, discovering great treasures at bargain prices.

What began as an experimental venture in 2019 quickly blossomed into a community success story. After the initial West Side store proved highly successful, it expanded to a larger location on Watts Road in 2020. Responding to strong community demand, a second, even larger East Side store opened on High Crossing Blvd in 2024, doubling the shopping experience. This growth underscores the community's commitment to supporting animal welfare through sustainable retail.

By shopping, donating, or volunteering at the Dane County Humane Society Thrift Store, patrons contribute directly to the well-being of animals in need across Dane County. Each purchase helps fund critical programs, from adoptions and wildlife rehabilitation to community outreach and pet surrender resources, making a tangible difference in the lives of countless creatures.

data.Title: Dane County Humane Society
data.Description:
The Dane County Humane Society (DCHS) is a dedicated animal welfare organization in Madison, WI, committed to its mission of "Helping People Help Animals." DCHS provides a wide array of essential services designed to support both domestic pets and local wildlife within the community. Their core offerings include facilitating pet adoptions, providing a safe haven for surrendered animals, and actively working to reunite lost pets with their families.

Beyond direct animal care, DCHS operates a crucial Wildlife Center, specializing in the rehabilitation of injured and orphaned wild animals with the goal of returning them to their natural habitats. The organization also fosters a compassionate community through humane education programs for all ages, behavior and training classes for dogs, and community support initiatives like Pets for Life, which offers vital resources to families. Through volunteering, fostering, and their Thrift Store, Dane County Humane Society empowers individuals to contribute to animal well-being, ensuring a thriving environment for all creatures.

data.Title: Dane County Juvenile Shelter
data.Description:
The Dane County Juvenile Shelter provides essential non-secure residential services for juveniles in Madison, WI, who require temporary placement pending further court action. Designed for youth aged 10-17, the shelter offers a safe and structured environment for up to 16 residents (8 boys and 8 girls) when a secure detention setting is not necessary. Stays can last up to 60 days, or 20 days if residents are transitioning between placements.

The shelter ensures a supportive atmosphere with 24-hour male and female staff supervision. Residents are encouraged to maintain their education, either by continuing their enrollment in Madison schools or participating in the Shelter Home School program, which provides an MMSD teacher. Medical care is prioritized, with health screens provided and efforts made to address residents' well-being. A structured daily routine includes opportunities to earn privileges, such as sign-out options, through good behavior and completion of household responsibilities.

Family involvement is supported through reasonable visiting hours and the possibility of home visits, coordinated with case managers. The program focuses on providing stability and a nurturing environment during a critical period, without billing parents for the placement. This comprehensive approach helps ensure the welfare and continued development of the youth in its care.

data.Title: Dane County Library Service
data.Description:
Dane County Library Service (DCLS) is dedicated to ensuring equitable access to comprehensive library services for all residents of Dane County, Wisconsin. Established in 1966, DCLS is renowned for its innovative mobile library programs, including the Bookmobile, Readmobile, and Dream Bus. These vital services deliver essential library resources directly to communities, cities, towns, and villages that lack a traditional public library, effectively bridging gaps in access and fostering a love for reading and learning across the county.

Beyond its extensive mobile fleet, DCLS offers a wide array of specialized outreach services designed to meet the unique needs of diverse populations. These include the Home Service Program for homebound individuals, Talking Books for those with physical reading limitations, and dedicated library services for children in day care facilities, nursing homes, assisted living facilities, senior centers, and the Dane County Jails. DCLS also provides digital resources like hoopla and engages the community with programs such as Spanish Storytime, reinforcing its commitment to comprehensive and inclusive library support throughout Dane County.

data.Title: Dane County Veterans Service Office (CVSO)
data.Description:
The Dane County Veterans Service Office (CVSO) in Madison, WI, is dedicated to advocating for and assisting Dane County veterans and their families in navigating and securing a wide array of local, state, and federal veterans benefits. Operating under Wis. Stat. § 48.50, the CVSO provides crucial support, from determining benefit eligibility to completing complex applications, ensuring veterans receive the entitlements they have earned. Their mission emphasizes customer service and compassionate engagement, recognizing that every veteran's story is unique.

The office boasts a team of eight dedicated, VA-accredited professionals, many of whom are veterans themselves, bringing firsthand understanding and expertise to their roles. They offer comprehensive assistance across numerous categories, including support for recently discharged veterans with health care enrollment and state benefits, aid for disabled veterans with compensation claims and appeals, and guidance for seniors on Wisconsin Veterans Homes and pensions. Additionally, the CVSO helps with education benefits like the GI Bill, home loan eligibility, various health benefits, and critical support during times of death, such as survivor's pensions and burial assistance.

Beyond direct benefit claims, the Dane County CVSO provides valuable "Other Services" like obtaining military records and awards, offering grave-care payments, and facilitating programs such as "Vets Ride With Pride" bus passes and referrals to affordable housing. Their accreditations with national organizations like the American Legion and Disabled American Veterans, alongside memberships in state and local veterans' associations, underscore their commitment to professional and effective advocacy for the veteran community.

data.Title: Department of Veterans Affairs
data.Description:
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is dedicated to providing comprehensive support and benefits to Veterans, service members, and their families. As a vital federal agency, the VA offers a wide array of services designed to enhance the well-being and quality of life for those who have served our nation. These include essential health care services, disability compensation for service-connected conditions, and robust education benefits like the GI Bill to support academic and vocational training.

Beyond these core offerings, the VA assists with career and employment services, pension programs for eligible wartime Veterans, and housing assistance through VA-backed home loans and grants. They also provide life insurance options, support for burial and memorial planning, and access to important military records. The VA empowers beneficiaries to manage their benefits and care online, ensuring convenient access to resources and information. Through its extensive network and programs, the Department of Veterans Affairs strives to honor the commitment of our Veterans by delivering the care and benefits they have earned.

data.Title: Door Creek Church - Northside Madison Campus
data.Description:
Door Creek Church - Northside Madison Campus offers a welcoming spiritual home in Madison, WI, providing a vibrant community for worship and growth. Located at 1181 N Sherman Ave, this campus hosts in-person Sunday services at 10:30 AM, featuring relevant Bible messages and opportunities for connection. Led by Pastor David Smith, who serves as the Northside Campus, Care & Outreach Pastor, the church emphasizes fostering strong relationships and supporting its members.

Beyond Sunday worship, the Northside Madison Campus provides a wide array of programs designed to engage all ages and stages of life. Families can benefit from dedicated DCC Kids programming available in-person, ensuring children have a fun and enriching experience. Adults are encouraged to join various small groups, Bible studies, and classes, offered both in-person and online, to deepen their faith and build meaningful connections within the community.

The campus is committed to holistic spiritual development and active involvement. Members can explore numerous ministries focusing on students, serving the community, personal growth, and care and support. With a strong emphasis on accessibility and a desire to connect, Door Creek Church - Northside Madison Campus invites individuals to discover a supportive environment where they can study God's Word, find community, and get involved in meaningful ways.

data.Title: Downtown Madison Inc
data.Description:
Downtown Madison Inc (DMI) is a not-for-profit advocacy organization dedicated to fostering a healthy, thriving, and vibrant downtown Madison, WI. For over 40 years, DMI has represented the interests of its 570+ members, including businesses, residents, and employees, ensuring the urban core remains an exceptional place to live, work, play, and visit. Its mission is to make Downtown Madison economically strong, inclusive, equitable, and vibrant for all.

DMI has been instrumental in the revitalization and ongoing development of downtown Madison. Key achievements include advocating for iconic projects like the Monona Terrace and Overture Center, establishing the Central Business Improvement District, and initiating popular community events such as the Dane County Farmers’ Market, Paddle & Portage, and Frostiball. The organization actively engages in research, planning, and community action through various committees focused on economic development, government relations, inclusivity, quality of life, and transportation.

Through its diverse event series, reports like the "State of the Downtown," and tools such as the Development Tracker and Data Dashboard, DMI continuously works to gather insights, facilitate connections, and drive progress. Committed to its values of respect, generosity, and diversity, DMI strives to build a downtown that is not only prosperous but also welcoming and accessible to everyone.

data.Title: Dryhootch
data.Description:
Dryhootch is a 501c3 nonprofit organization in Madison, WI, founded by combat Veterans to support their peers in returning home and navigating civilian life. Operating as a unique coffee house, Dryhootch provides a safe, comfortable, and entirely drug-and-alcohol-free environment where Veterans can gather informally, connect, and find camaraderie. The name "Dryhootch" signifies a "safe place" (hootch) that is free from alcohol, addressing a significant challenge many Veterans face.

The organization offers a comprehensive suite of peer-led support programs designed "by Veterans, for Veterans." These services include certified peer mentoring through its QRF Mobile program, readjustment assistance, legal aid, family support, addiction recovery groups, and creative outlets such as music, art, and writing. Dryhootch fosters a community where Veterans and their families can receive understanding, guidance, and resources, ensuring they "survive the peace" after their service.

Beyond direct support, Dryhootch also aims to encourage Veteran interaction with the broader community and supports an extended network of Veteran families. The coffee shop model serves as a central hub for these activities, providing a welcoming space for connection and healing.

data.Title: Eagle Heights Community Center
data.Description:
Eagle Heights Community Center, situated within the UW-Madison Eagle Heights Apartment community in Madison, WI, serves as a dynamic hub for graduate students, students with families, postdoctoral researchers, and university staff. As an essential component of University Housing's dedication to resident success, the center cultivates a welcoming and supportive environment tailored to the distinct needs of its diverse population. It provides crucial resources and programming designed to enhance community well-being, facilitate academic pursuits, and enrich family life for its residents.

The center offers a variety of services and dedicated spaces, including communal areas for social gatherings, quiet study rooms, and facilities for family-friendly activities and events. It plays a pivotal role in fostering connections among residents through organized workshops, cultural events, and robust support networks. By creating opportunities for engagement and mutual assistance, Eagle Heights Community Center helps residents integrate seamlessly into the broader UW-Madison community, ensuring a comprehensive and enriching living experience aligned with University Housing's core values of care, integrity, and stewardship.

data.Title: East Madison Community Center
data.Description:
The East Madison Community Center (EMCC) has served as a vital hub for families in Madison, WI's Truax neighborhood for over 59 years. Established in 1966, EMCC provides a safe and welcoming environment where residents can gather, learn, and support one another. The center is dedicated to empowering individuals to achieve their goals, gain valuable skills, and strengthen the community through a diverse array of programs.

As a thriving multi-service center, EMCC offers comprehensive social, educational, recreational, and cultural programming. These initiatives focus on key areas such as education, employment, fitness, and socialization, all designed to enhance the quality of life for individuals and the community as a whole. Supported by a dedicated team of staff and 250 volunteers, EMCC plays a crucial role in connecting residents with essential resources and fostering a sense of belonging. The organization prides itself on building brighter futures for local families through strong partnerships and a commitment to community service.

data.Title: Ebling Library for the Health Sciences
data.Description:
Ebling Library for the Health Sciences, located within the Health Sciences Learning Center at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, serves as a vital hub for health sciences education, research, and clinical practice. It provides comprehensive access to an extensive collection of specialized resources tailored for students, faculty, and staff across various health disciplines.

The library offers a rich array of databases, including essential tools like UpToDate, ClinicalKey, PubMed, and Scopus, alongside a vast selection of health sciences journals such as Academic Medicine, JAMA, and NEJM. Patrons can also access numerous e-books, including AccessMedicine and Harrison's. Beyond traditional resources, Ebling Library provides specialized topic guides covering areas from AI in Academic Health Sciences and Anatomy to Global Health and Systematic Reviews, supporting in-depth research and learning. The library also fosters a vibrant academic community through events, workshops, and cultural initiatives like its arts journal, Corpus Callosum, and various exhibitions.

data.Title: Eken Park Little Library
data.Description:
Eken Park Little Library in Madison, WI, is a cherished local book-sharing box, proudly operating as part of the global Little Free Library network. This volunteer-led initiative is dedicated to cultivating a love for reading and strengthening community bonds within the Eken Park neighborhood. Offering 24/7, free access to books for all ages, it effectively removes barriers to literacy and encourages neighbors to engage through the simple, yet profound, act of sharing stories.

Embodying the broader mission of expanding book access, Eken Park Little Library actively contributes to inspiring readers and promoting diverse voices. By providing a wide array of books, it fosters understanding, empathy, and inclusion, addressing local "book deserts" and ensuring that personally relevant literature is readily available. This local library plays a vital role in enhancing literacy outcomes and nurturing a lifelong passion for reading, making the Eken Park community a more connected and vibrant place, one book exchange at a time.

data.Title: Environment Control of Wisconsin, Inc.
data.Description:
Environment Control of Wisconsin, Inc. has been a trusted provider of commercial cleaning and janitorial services across Wisconsin for over 48 years, proudly owned and operated by Tom and Melody Hanson. With a deep commitment to consistent quality and customer satisfaction, they offer a comprehensive array of services tailored to meet diverse business needs and budgets. Their expertise spans general janitorial, specialized cleaning, and critical healthcare-grade disinfection, ensuring a pristine and healthy environment for offices, clinics, schools, warehouses, and high-tech facilities.

The organization excels in delivering customized cleaning plans, from routine janitorial and post-construction cleanups to carpet care, window washing, and green cleaning solutions. A key differentiator is their meticulous approach to recruiting, training, and proactive management of their 400+ diverse employees, fostering a team that is highly valued and dedicated to excellence. This focus on employee well-being directly translates into reliable, high-quality service for clients.

Environment Control of Wisconsin, Inc. promises an unbeatable value, providing peace of mind through total ownership of facility cleaning. They are dedicated to creating the cleanest possible work environment while maintaining fair compensation for their hard-working team.

data.Title: Environmental Construction Services Inc.
data.Description:
Environmental Construction Services Inc., based in Madison, WI, is a trusted full-service environmental contractor specializing in comprehensive solutions for industrial, commercial, governmental, educational, and residential clients. Since 2001, the company has been dedicated to providing safe and effective management of hazardous materials and demolition projects. Their core services include expert asbestos abatement, thorough mold remediation, and full-scale demolition, encompassing interior, total building, and job site cleaning.

Leveraging extensive experience in the field, Environmental Construction Services Inc. is committed to delivering timely, cost-effective, and responsible solutions tailored to each project's unique requirements. They pride themselves on ensuring customer satisfaction through quality service, whether it involves containment, removal, encapsulation of asbestos, or utilizing professional products and technology for mold remediation. Their Madison location allows for prompt response to environmental needs throughout Wisconsin.

data.Title: Extended Hands Food Pantry
data.Description:
Extended Hands Food Pantry is a volunteer-driven, faith-based non-profit organization in Madison, WI, dedicated to combating food insecurity and supporting community well-being. Our primary mission is to provide groceries and essential household items to individuals and families in need, with a strong emphasis on offering culturally appropriate foods to better serve diverse populations. Beyond food distribution, we are deeply committed to childhood nutrition and education, offering after-school meals and tutoring to children in low-income neighborhoods, recognizing the critical link between nourishment and academic success.

Founded by Andy and Jenny Czerkas, who have over 25 years of experience battling hunger in Madison, Extended Hands Pantry has seen remarkable growth, increasing visitors by 550% in five years. We serve Dane County's most vulnerable populations, including immigrants and refugees, ensuring every person can choose their own food in a respectful and dignified manner. Our comprehensive approach addresses immediate hunger while fostering long-term educational support, embodying compassionate acts of love and servant-hearted expression. We rely on community support through donations and volunteers to sustain our vital efforts.

data.Title: Faith Community Bible Church
data.Description:
Faith Community Bible Church is a vibrant and creative urban campus church located in the Regent Street area of Madison, WI, with over 40 years of history serving its community. This welcoming faith community is dedicated to living out the beauty and love of Jesus, inviting all who are seeking to join them. They are a mosaic of individuals, including teachers, artists, business professionals, and students, all intricately connected to the city, the UW campus, and God.

The church believes in making God's love known through their words, actions, gifts, and talents, fostering a loving environment for everyone in the neighborhood. They embrace a team-led approach to ministry, with various teams overseeing leadership, teaching, musical worship, and small house groups for deeper community engagement. Faith Community Bible Church focuses on bringing God's presence into their daily lives and sharing it with Madison.

data.Title: First United Methodist Church
data.Description:
First United Methodist Church in Madison, WI, serves as a vibrant spiritual hub dedicated to fostering faith, community, and service. This welcoming church offers diverse worship experiences, including weekly in-person and online services, alongside special "Come As You Are" worship opportunities. Beyond Sunday worship, the church actively engages its members and the wider Madison community through a rich array of programs designed for all ages and stages of life.

The church emphasizes spiritual growth and community involvement, providing extensive ministries for children, youth, young adults, adults, and seniors. Educational initiatives like the Lyons Lecture Series and a comprehensive church library support lifelong learning. First United Methodist Church is also deeply committed to outreach, exemplified by its Hope’s Home Outreach Ministries and Adopt-a-School partnerships, offering numerous volunteer opportunities for those seeking to make a tangible difference. With a focus on worship, music, arts, and compassionate service, the church strives to be a place where individuals can connect, grow, and contribute to a more just and loving world.

data.Title: Forward Theater at Overture
data.Description:
Forward Theater Company, based in Madison, Wisconsin, is a premier professional theater organization dedicated to delivering exceptional theatrical experiences that resonate with local audiences. Founded in 2009, Forward Theater not only showcases a diverse lineup of contemporary and Broadway-inspired plays but also fosters a vibrant artistic community by providing a home for local artists. The theater is committed to the Wisconsin Idea, emphasizing community engagement through pre-show lectures and post-show discussions, enriching the audience's connection to the performances.

What sets Forward Theater apart is its dedication to accessibility and inclusivity, ensuring that all community members can enjoy the transformative power of live theater. With a focus on fresh and thought-provoking narratives, the company regularly collaborates with notable playwrights and engages in initiatives like the Writer in Residence program, which nurtures new works and innovative storytelling. By combining high-quality productions with an emphasis on audience interaction and educational outreach, Forward Theater cultivates a unique cultural hub in Madison, making it an essential destination for theater enthusiasts and newcomers alike.

data.Title: Freedom, Inc.
data.Description:
Freedom, Inc. is a Madison, WI-based social justice organization dedicated to fostering liberation and empowerment within Black, Hmong, and Cambodian communities. Operating under the guiding principle that "our community is our campaign," the organization drives culturally specific programming and advocacy to address systemic inequities and build collective strength.

A core pillar of their work is Gender Justice, where they provide critical support for women experiencing domestic violence and sexual assault. This encompasses essential services such as legal aid, crisis intervention, housing assistance, economic advocacy, and safety planning, ensuring comprehensive and culturally responsive care for survivors. Concurrently, Freedom, Inc. deeply integrates Queer Justice into all its endeavors, offering specialized programming for queer people of color to ensure freedom and equity for individuals of all gender and sexual identities, recognizing the unique challenges faced by these communities.

Their commitment extends to Black and Southeast Asian Liberation, where programming and social justice initiatives are meticulously tailored to the distinct needs and cultural heritage of Black, Hmong, and Cambodian individuals. By building strength from within these communities, Freedom, Inc. provides vital resources and advocacy, working towards a more just and equitable society for all.

data.Title: Gates of Heaven
data.Description:
Gates of Heaven in Madison, WI, offers a unique and historic venue for intimate events, particularly wedding ceremonies. Originally built in 1863, it stands as the fourth oldest surviving synagogue building in the United States, meticulously moved to James Madison Park in 1971. This beautifully preserved Victorian-era structure provides a distinctive backdrop, blending historical charm with modern conveniences for memorable gatherings.

The venue is available year-round and features seating for approximately 98 guests, along with essential amenities such as restrooms, water, ample lighting, electrical outlets, and central air and heat. While food and beverages (other than water) are generally prohibited, exceptions are made for alcohol during religious ceremonies with a required permit. Its prime location within James Madison Park also offers access to picturesque Victorian-era Period Gardens, ideal for stunning photographs.

Managed by the City of Madison Parks Division, Gates of Heaven is cherished for its rich history and elegant simplicity. It is a sought-after choice for those seeking a meaningful and intimate setting for their special occasions, ensuring a comfortable and unique experience for all attendees.

data.Title: Goodman Community Center Brass Works Building
data.Description:
The Goodman Community Center Brass Works Building, located in Madison, WI, serves as a vital component of the larger Goodman Community Center campus. As one of two beautiful, historic buildings, Brass Works contributes significantly to the center's enduring mission of strengthening lives and securing futures for the Madison community, a commitment upheld since 1954. This cherished resource provides a welcoming and dynamic space where diverse programs and essential services unfold daily.

Within the Brass Works Building and across the Goodman campus, individuals of all ages find abundant opportunities for connection, courage, and curiosity. The facility supports innovative, research-based programs for preschoolers through teens, fostering essential life skills, and keeps older adults engaged and connected through various activities. It also functions as a vibrant hub for community gatherings, hosting celebrations, meetings, and classes for families, businesses, and organizations from across the Greater Madison area. The Brass Works Building, alongside its sister Ironworks, embodies the spirit of community, making Goodman a special place where lives are enriched in meaningful ways through access to resources like food security and fitness opportunities.

data.Title: Grace Episcopal Church
data.Description:
Grace Episcopal Church, prominently situated on Madison's Capitol Square, is a vibrant and inclusive faith community dedicated to sharing the love of Jesus Christ through worship and extensive outreach. Rooted in Anglican tradition, Grace Church warmly welcomes all individuals, explicitly affirming its commitment to LGBTQ+ inclusion, fostering a beloved and accepting environment for everyone on their spiritual journey.

Beyond its regular worship services, including Holy Eucharist and Christian Formation, Grace Church is deeply embedded in the Madison community through a wide array of ministries. For over 50 years, its Grace Food Pantry has provided essential support to those in need. The church actively engages in social justice initiatives like "Creating a More Just Community," addressing issues of racial justice and mass incarceration, and offers its "Grace's Space" for public witness and community dialogue.

Grace Church also enriches the cultural life of Madison with its renowned music program, featuring a Chancel Choir, a fine pipe organ, and the "Grace Presents" concert series. Its historic building and English-style courtyard garden also serve as a distinctive venue for weddings. Through these diverse offerings, Grace Episcopal Church stands as a beacon of care, compassion, and community engagement in downtown Madison.

data.Title: Grants Information Collection
data.Description:
The Grants Information Collection (GIC) in Madison, WI, is a vital resource for individuals and organizations seeking funding. As a proud Funding Information Network partner of Candid (formerly the Foundation Center), the GIC provides comprehensive access to information on grants, philanthropy, and charitable giving. Its mission is to enhance research, advance learning, and support nonprofit initiatives across Wisconsin, serving both university affiliates and the broader community.

The GIC offers a rich array of resources for grants research, including dedicated onsite computer workstations and remote access to powerful databases like Foundation Directory Online Quick Start. UW-Madison affiliates also benefit from specialized access to Pivot and other subscription funding tools. The collection provides extensive support for various funding needs, from education and research to nonprofit and specific organizational grants, complemented by grant proposal resources and helpful tutorials. It's important to note that the GIC functions purely as an information provider and does not manage or distribute grants.

Visitors can leverage the expertise of the Grants Librarian for personalized assistance, ensuring they can effectively navigate the vast landscape of funding opportunities. The GIC is committed to making complex grant information accessible, empowering users to find the resources they need to achieve their philanthropic and research goals.

data.Title: Great Plains Paleontology
data.Description:
Great Plains Paleontology, based in Madison, WI, is led by sole proprietor Craig Pfister, who specializes in the discovery, excavation, preparation, and sale of authentic dinosaur fossils. Unlike many commercial fossil dealers, Great Plains Paleontology prides itself on sourcing all specimens directly through its own expeditions, ensuring a unique and verifiable provenance for each piece. Every fossil is meticulously prepared to museum-quality standards, reflecting a deep commitment to scientific integrity and preservation.

The organization operates with the highest ethical standards, collecting all fossils legally from private land with explicit landowner consent. Landowners are actively involved, kept informed throughout the excavation and sale process, and receive a percentage of the final sale price. This transparent and responsible approach guarantees that clients acquire not just a fossil, but a piece of natural history collected with care and respect.

Great Plains Paleontology's commitment to excellence is further evidenced by its impressive track record, with specimens housed in prestigious institutions worldwide, including the Museum für Naturkunde in Berlin, the Royal Ontario Museum in Toronto, and the Melbourne Victoria Museum. This demonstrates the exceptional quality and scientific significance of the fossils offered, making Great Plains Paleontology a trusted source for collectors and institutions seeking genuine, museum-grade dinosaur specimens.

data.Title: Greater Madison Chamber of Commerce
data.Description:
The Greater Madison Chamber of Commerce stands as the preeminent business voice for the Madison, Wisconsin community, dedicated to fostering prosperity and opportunity that drives community wealth and helps the region reach its full potential. Central to its mission is the "Beam" platform, which strategically focuses on four pillars: defining and amplifying the region's brand, driving economic growth through initiatives and resources, advocating for business interests at all levels of government, and connecting members to invaluable resources and new opportunities.

The Chamber is deeply committed to empowering its diverse membership, recognizing them as the leaders and innovators shaping Greater Madison's economic future. It provides a robust framework for businesses to thrive, offering networking events, a comprehensive business directory, and specialized programs like DIJE and LGM. By leveraging the collective strength of its members and championing innovation, the Greater Madison Chamber of Commerce plays a crucial role in building a dynamic and prosperous business environment for the entire community.

data.Title: Groundswell Conservancy
data.Description:
Groundswell Conservancy is a results-oriented, community-based nonprofit organization dedicated to permanently protecting special places in south-central Wisconsin since 1983. They work to ensure everyone has equitable access to the benefits of land and nature, fostering physical, emotional, and spiritual wellness. Their comprehensive approach addresses critical environmental issues, including acting on the climate crisis, conserving vital wildlife habitat, and connecting people with the outdoors.

The Conservancy partners with farm families to preserve rich agricultural soils for future generations, helps elementary schools in Madison create green schoolyards, and manages natural areas for wildlife. A key focus is improving access and land tenure for farmers of color and New American farmers, demonstrating a strong commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion. Through these efforts, Groundswell Conservancy has protected hundreds of significant natural and agricultural sites, ensuring their preservation forever.

data.Title: Group Health Cooperative
data.Description:
Group Health Cooperative of South Central Wisconsin (GHC-SCW) is a pioneering non-profit, member-owned health plan that has been dedicated to providing high-quality health care for over 49 years. Serving approximately 70,000 members, GHC-SCW uniquely integrates health care and health insurance, ensuring that members receive comprehensive and coordinated services. As the first Health Maintenance Organization (HMO) in Dane County, GHC-SCW has established itself as a trusted leader in the region, focusing on maximizing health and well-being through community partnerships and member-centered care.

GHC-SCW stands out for its commitment to health equity, inclusivity, and innovation, grounded in core values that prioritize quality-driven service and community involvement. The organization’s strategic pillars emphasize exceptional quality and service, meaningful employee engagement, and adaptive transformation to meet the evolving needs of its members. With a strong belief that health care is a human right, GHC-SCW fosters a welcoming environment where diversity is celebrated, ensuring that all voices are heard and respected. Members benefit from a wide range of services, including accessible behavioral health programs, virtual care options, and a robust network of in-clinic providers, all designed to promote lifelong health and well-being in the communities served.

data.Title: Harvest Church of Madison
data.Description:
Harvest Church of Madison is a vibrant Presbyterian Church in America (PCA) affiliated congregation committed to sharing the hope of the gospel within Madison, WI, and extending its reach beyond. Guided by their vision to "gather, grow, and go as workers for the harvest," the church firmly adheres to the inspired Word of God and the foundational principles of Christian faith, as faithfully summarized in the Westminster Confession of Faith. This commitment ensures a robust theological grounding for all its ministries and teachings.

The church offers a welcoming and enriching environment for individuals and families seeking spiritual growth and community. Sunday services are a central gathering point, available both in-person and virtually, featuring worship and Gospel-centered teaching designed to uplift and instruct. A dedicated Children's Church program provides a joyful and nurturing space where young ones learn about God through engaging activities and Bible study. Additionally, active men's and women's ministries organize various events throughout the year, providing further opportunities for spiritual development and building strong relationships within the congregation.

data.Title: Healthy Minds Innovations
data.Description:
Healthy Minds Innovations, now operating as Humin, is a Madison, WI-based global nonprofit dedicated to advancing human flourishing by translating rigorous wellbeing science into practical, accessible tools and programs. Founded on the pioneering neuroscientific research of Richard J. Davidson and in collaboration with the Center for Healthy Minds at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, the organization develops evidence-based solutions designed to cultivate mental and emotional wellbeing.

Their offerings include the acclaimed Healthy Minds Program app, providing free, science-backed training to millions worldwide, and the Kindness Curriculum, an Emmy-winning educational program that instills compassion in children. Beyond individual resources, Healthy Minds Innovations (Humin) partners with organizations to embed wellbeing science, enhancing performance, resilience, and overall potential across diverse sectors. Driven by a mission to make wellbeing real for everyone, they aim to create a kinder, wiser, and more compassionate world through scalable, impactful interventions.

data.Title: Highland Manor Park - Storm Shelter
data.Description:
Highland Manor Park - Storm Shelter in Madison, WI, provides a versatile and essential community facility. This reservable shelter, located at 10 Manor Drive within Highland Manor Park, is available year-round for various events and gatherings. It boasts a maximum capacity of 212 people, with seating provided for approximately 100 guests across 20 folding tables and stackable chairs. The shelter is equipped with convenient amenities including in-shelter restrooms, accessible water, and a dedicated parking lot featuring 26 standard and 2 accessible stalls, with additional overflow parking available on Moorland Road. A PA (amplified sound) permit is also allowed for up to six hours, ending by 9 p.m., making it suitable for diverse activities.

Beyond its function as a reservable event space, Highland Manor Park - Storm Shelter serves a critical dual role as a community safe room. During periods of inclement weather, the facility transforms into a secure location for neighboring residents seeking refuge from severe storms. This commitment to public safety ensures that the community has a designated safe haven when emergencies arise. In instances where a reservation is impacted by the facility's use as an emergency shelter, the reserving party is guaranteed a full refund.

This unique combination of a well-equipped reservable shelter and a vital community storm safe room makes Highland Manor Park - Storm Shelter a cornerstone asset for the Madison community, supporting both recreational needs and public safety during severe weather events.

data.Title: Hillel at the University of Wisconsin
data.Description:
Hillel at the University of Wisconsin serves as the vibrant hub for Jewish life on the UW-Madison campus, dedicated to fostering a strong sense of community, identity, and belonging. Through its core mission to "Connect. Lead. Grow.," UW Hillel provides a welcoming and inclusive environment where students can explore and celebrate their Jewish heritage. The organization offers a rich tapestry of intentionally crafted programming, events, services, and holiday celebrations designed to engage students at every stage of their university journey.

From lively Shabbat dinners and meaningful holiday observances to social gatherings and leadership opportunities, UW Hillel ensures that Jewish students find a supportive "home away from home" in the bustling university setting. It actively connects current, incoming, and prospective students, as well as their families and the broader community, to a dynamic Jewish experience. By offering diverse avenues for engagement, UW Hillel empowers students to build lasting friendships, develop leadership skills, and deepen their connection to Jewish traditions and values, making the large campus feel smaller and more personal.

data.Title: Ho-Chunk Nation Madison Youth
data.Description:
Ho-Chunk Nation Madison Youth, operating as the Madison Youth & Learning Center, serves as a vital community hub dedicated to the development and well-being of young tribal members in Madison, WI. Rooted in the rich cultural heritage and oral traditions of the Ho-Chunk Nation, this center provides a supportive environment for youth to thrive. It embodies the Nation's commitment to passing along traditions to younger generations, ensuring a strong foundation for their future.

The center aims to empower Ho-Chunk youth through various programs and resources, fostering educational achievement, cultural understanding, and personal growth. While specific program details are not outlined, the presence of a co-located Behavioral Health office at the same address suggests a holistic approach to youth support, addressing both mental and emotional well-being alongside learning and cultural immersion. The Madison Youth & Learning Center plays a crucial role in connecting young people to their heritage and community.

As part of the larger Ho-Chunk Nation, which emphasizes the safety and well-being of its citizens, the Madison Youth & Learning Center contributes to a comprehensive network of services designed to support tribal members across all life stages. It stands as a testament to the Nation's enduring presence and its dedication to nurturing the next generation of "People of the Big Voice."

data.Title: Housing Initiatives
data.Description:
Housing Initiatives is Madison, WI's only organization exclusively dedicated to ending homelessness for individuals living with severe mental illness. For over 30 years, the organization has provided safe, permanent homes and comprehensive supportive services, achieving a remarkable 95% success rate where clients never return to homelessness. Their highly effective "Housing First" model prioritizes stable housing as the foundation for healing and recovery, recognizing that a permanent home is crucial for mental and physical well-being.

Built on principles of dignity, respect, and a supportive approach to healing, Housing Initiatives connects clients with over 15 partner agencies for vital support, including counseling, substance abuse programs, and medication therapy. Their neighborhood-based housing model places clients in small apartment buildings throughout Madison, fostering community reintegration and access to essential city services, empowering them to live independently.

Beyond transforming individual lives, Housing Initiatives significantly benefits the Madison community by rebuilding lives, fostering re-engagement with employment and family. Their cost-effective model saves taxpayers money, costing $10,000 per person annually compared to $40,000 for traditional homelessness support. Additionally, they enrich neighborhoods by renovating properties, spurring development and extending stability throughout the area.

data.Title: IPM Institute of North America
data.Description:
The IPM Institute of North America, based in Madison, WI, is an independent non-profit established in 1998 with a mission to enhance sustainability in agriculture and communities. With over 25 years of experience, the Institute specializes in Integrated Pest Management (IPM), focusing on reducing pesticide use and risks. Their expertise has expanded to encompass a broad range of agricultural sustainability issues, addressing critical areas such as improving working conditions, reducing greenhouse gases, enhancing air and water quality, and promoting soil health.

Leveraging the power of the marketplace, the IPM Institute collaborates with food and agricultural companies across the entire supply chain, from growers to retailers. They develop and implement impactful tools, strategies, and certifications like Green Shield Certified and the Sustainability Standard. Their work is structured through branches such as the Sustainable Food Group and Sustainable Communities Group, offering specialized services and certifications to drive positive environmental and health outcomes. The Institute is dedicated to turning ideas into action, fostering a world where food production and community practices are in sync with natural processes.

data.Title: Isaiah Church
data.Description:
Isaiah Church is a vibrant Christian community in Madison, WI, dedicated to exalting Jesus Christ and proclaiming the profound truth of the gospel. They gather for worship services every Sunday at 10 AM at the Madison Marriott South Hotel, providing a welcoming environment for individuals and families to grow in faith. The church's core mission revolves around the belief that Jesus came, died, and rose again to reconcile sinners to God, forming the foundation of all their teachings and activities.

Committed to making authentic disciples, Isaiah Church offers a range of ministries designed to foster spiritual growth and community engagement. These include dedicated programs for children, specialized support for college students, and various small groups for deeper fellowship and study. The church also hosts regular events, encouraging members to connect and serve together. Through powerful sermons, community outreach, and intentional discipleship, Isaiah Church strives to impact Madison with the transformative message of Christ.

data.Title: Islamic Center of Madison
data.Description:
The Islamic Center of Madison, located in the heart of Madison, WI, next to the University of Wisconsin Campus, stands as the oldest of the three mosques in the area. Established by university students, it serves as a vital hub for the local Muslim population, particularly those associated with the university, providing a dedicated space for the five daily prayers and fostering a close-knit community. Its core mission is to carry out religious, charitable, and educational activities in full conformity with Islamic principles.

The Center offers a diverse range of programs and services designed to enrich the spiritual and social lives of its members. These include regular congregational prayers, a weekly Islamic school for children, free Quran classes for adults, and special events like Eid al-Fitr celebrations. Beyond religious observance, the Islamic Center of Madison actively engages in community support through initiatives such as Food Pantry Wednesdays and monthly gatherings for Muslim women, embodying a spirit of brotherhood and mutual assistance.

data.Title: Isthmus Dance Collective
data.Description: Isthmus Dance Collective is a Madison-based nonprofit organization dedicated to making dance accessible and welcoming for the community. The collective brings together dancers, choreographers, and educators to present performances, workshops, and collaborative projects that celebrate creativity, movement, and artistic expression. Through community engagement and inclusive programming, the organization encourages participation from people of diverse ages, abilities, and experience levels while supporting the growth of dance as a vibrant part of Madison's arts community.

data.Title: Jewish Experience of Madison - JEM
data.Description:
Jewish Experience of Madison (JEM) serves as a vibrant and welcoming "home away from home" for Jewish students in Madison, WI. Dedicated to fostering a strong sense of community and personal growth, JEM provides a supportive environment where students can relax, decompress, and authentically explore their Jewish identity.

The organization offers enriching programs designed to connect students with Jewish life and each other. Signature offerings include the Maimonides Fellowship, a 10-week program featuring weekly talks, dinners, and discussions aimed at intellectual and spiritual development, complete with a stipend. Additionally, JEM hosts highly anticipated Shabbat dinners, known for their great people, inviting vibe, and delicious food, creating memorable experiences and fostering deep connections.

JEM is committed to creating an inclusive space where students feel comfortable, inspired, and engaged. Through its diverse activities and warm atmosphere, JEM empowers individuals to actualize their most authentic selves, build lasting friendships, and engage in thought-provoking conversations that help shape their personal and Jewish journeys.

data.Title: Kennedy Heights Community Center
data.Description:
Kennedy Heights Community Center (KHCC) is a vital non-profit organization in Madison, WI, dedicated to fostering a strong community support network for low to moderate-income families. Established from a grassroots initiative by residents concerned about youth activities and community well-being, KHCC has grown significantly since its incorporation in 1986. The center's mission is to enhance the lives of residents by increasing available resources and offering a diverse array of social, educational, recreational, and cultural programs for children, youth, and adults.

KHCC provides essential services designed to meet the evolving needs of the Madison community. A key offering is its public Food Pantry, which serves over 55 households weekly, directly addressing food insecurity. Beyond immediate needs, the center actively engages youth through programs like its Middle School initiative, creating a positive and supportive environment. Through its comprehensive programming, Kennedy Heights Community Center empowers individuals, strengthens family units, and builds a more vibrant and connected neighborhood.

data.Title: Lussier Family East YMCA
data.Description:
The Lussier Family East YMCA, a cornerstone of the Madison community, is a dedicated branch of the YMCA of Dane County, committed to its overarching mission of fostering youth development, promoting healthy living, and encouraging social responsibility. Located at 711 Cottage Grove Rd, this facility serves as a vibrant hub where individuals and families can thrive.

As part of a national nonprofit organization with a rich history, the Lussier Family East YMCA offers a comprehensive range of programs designed to strengthen the mind, body, and spirit. Members have access to diverse activities, including engaging sports leagues, essential swimming lessons, reliable childcare services, and a variety of invigorating group fitness classes for all ages and abilities.

The Y's inclusive environment ensures that everyone feels welcome and supported in their journey towards personal growth and community engagement. By providing these vital resources, the Lussier Family East YMCA actively contributes to building a healthier, more connected, and more resilient Madison.

data.Title: Luther Memorial Church
data.Description:
Luther Memorial Church in Madison, WI, is an intergenerational faith community affiliated with the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America (ELCA). Founded in 1907 by Lutheran UW students, it stands as a welcoming and inclusive "Reconciling in Christ" congregation, embodying the belief that "the liturgy lives and Christ welcomes all."

The church offers traditional Holy Communion services on Sundays at 8:15 am and 10:30 am, with the latter also livestreamed. Beyond worship, Luther Memorial provides extensive learning opportunities, including Bible studies, Sunday School, and Confirmation programs for all ages. Its vibrant music ministry features Bach Cantatas, multiple choirs, and impressive pipe organs, enriching the worship experience and cultural life.

Committed to community and social justice, Luther Memorial actively supports initiatives like The Keep Food Pantry, serving local university students and faculty. The church also fosters a strong sense of belonging through various groups, retreats, and a dedicated Youth & Family Ministry. Furthermore, its partnership with Parroquia Santa Maria extends its welcoming embrace to the Spanish-speaking community, offering worship and programs in Spanish.

data.Title: Madison Baptist Church
data.Description:
Madison Baptist Church has been a spiritual cornerstone in Madison, WI, for over 60 years, dedicated to "Taking the Word to the World." Led by Senior Pastor Mike Weiss, the church offers a welcoming environment for individuals and families seeking to grow in their faith and connect with a vibrant community. data.Description:

Unlike traditional sanctions-based approaches, MJTC employs intensive therapy to address the root causes of behavior, decompressing cycles of punishment and promoting positive change. The center provides comprehensive care, encouragement, treatment, and education, focusing on building trust to cultivate more acceptable choices, personal esteem, and autonomy.

MJTC's program includes individual and group activities and classes designed to help patients accept responsibility, develop social and problem-solving skills, resolve mental health issues, and build healthy relationships. The ultimate goal is to successfully reintegrate these young individuals into their communities. Research studies have demonstrated that youth treated at MJTC commit significantly fewer crimes post-release compared to similar youth who did not access the program.

Serving both boys and girls, MJTC expanded its campus to accommodate a larger patient population, with a capacity for 94 patients (74 boys and 20 girls) across nine specialized units. Patients are transferred from the youth justice system, including Lincoln Hills School, Copper Lake School, or county-run secure residential care centers, ensuring specialized treatment tailored to their security needs and responsiveness.

They foster an environment where everyone is genuinely welcome, regardless of age, background, or spiritual journey, whether skeptical or a lifelong believer.

The church emphasizes real connection and spiritual growth, encouraging members to engage in practices like weekly worship, community groups, Sabbath rest, and prayer. Beyond internal growth, New Culture Church is committed to actively contributing to the renewal of Madison through local service projects and community engagement. They provide a supportive, family-like atmosphere where individuals can explore their faith, ask questions, and experience a transformative relationship with Jesus, finding belonging and purpose.

data.Title: New Life Church
data.Description:
New Life Church in Madison, WI, offers a vibrant and welcoming community for individuals seeking a place to belong, serve, and find purpose. Distinguishing itself through genuine hospitality and a commitment to diversity, New Life embraces all who are on a faith journey, whether lifelong followers, doubters, or those just beginning. The church encourages active participation, providing opportunities for service within the congregation and the wider community to make a real difference in Jesus' name.

With a rich history dating back to 1955 as St. Matthew's Lutheran Church, New Life has evolved while maintaining its core values of hospitality, forgiveness, and grace. Today, it provides diverse worship experiences, including an energetic Contemporary Praise Service with a full band, a Traditional Praise Service for those preferring classic Lutheran worship, and even outdoor Parking Lot Worship. For those unable to attend in person, services are live-streamed on Facebook and available on YouTube, ensuring accessibility and continued connection to faith and community. New Life Church is dedicated to guiding parishioners on their path of faith, fostering a stimulating and contemporary environment rooted in the principles of Jesus.

data.Title: NewBridge Madison- North
data.Description:
NewBridge Madison- North is a leading non-profit organization dedicated to providing older adults in Madison, WI, with a bridge to successful aging. For over 50 years, NewBridge has been committed to ensuring longer, healthier, and safer independent lives through a comprehensive suite of services. These include vital support such as Case Management, Home Chore assistance, Food Bridge programs, Foot Care Clinics, Guardianship & Representative Payee services, and Mental Health Resources.

The organization also offers enriching Activities for All, with specific initiatives for Black and Hispanic Older Adults, alongside Nutrition programs and a dedicated "Ending Isolation Madison" initiative to foster connection and community. NewBridge Madison- North is deeply committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, actively promoting antiracism and creating an LGBTQ+ friendly, welcoming environment for all participants, including immigrant neighbors. They provide services in Spanish and ensure access regardless of status, language, or family situation.

NewBridge Madison- North strives to create a community where every older adult feels seen, valued, and connected, offering free services based on income to maximize accessibility and impact. Their holistic approach addresses various needs, empowering older adults to thrive independently within their community.

data.Title: Northside Christian Assembly
data.Description:
Northside Christian Assembly in Madison, WI, is a vibrant spiritual community dedicated to helping individuals discover hope, purpose, and belonging. They offer engaging in-person Sunday services at 10 AM, providing a welcoming and inspiring environment for worship, spiritual growth, and connection. The assembly emphasizes fostering a supportive atmosphere where attendees can deepen their faith journey.

Beyond weekly gatherings, Northside Christian Assembly provides multiple avenues for engagement and spiritual development. Members can access a rich library of sermons online, utilize the NCA Church App for convenient content access, and take "Next Steps" to integrate more deeply into the church community.
